GA4 with Cookie Compliance

Cookbook · guide · Last verified 25 November 2026 · View raw markdown (for agents)

In short: keep the Cookie Compliance snippet as the first script in <head>, then paste Google's GA4 tag below it. The banner holds the recognised Google loader until the visitor allows Content Personalisation, in regions whose rule requires consent first.

You need #

  • The Cookie Compliance snippet already installed as the first script in <head> (see plain-html or your platform guide).
  • Your GA4 Measurement ID (G-XXXX) and Google's standard tag from the Google Analytics admin.
  • Edit access to the same template, theme or head field as the banner snippet.

Where it goes #

Google's docs place the standard tag immediately after the opening <head> tag. With Cookie Compliance installed, keep the banner snippet first, then paste the GA4 tag below it — same shape Google gives you:

<!-- Cookie Compliance snippet first, then: -->
<script async src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-XXXX"></script>
<script>
  window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
  function gtag(){dataLayer.push(arguments);}
  gtag('js', new Date());
  gtag('config', 'G-XXXX');
</script>

Firing GA4 through Google Tag Manager instead? Put the banner above the GTM container and gate tags with consent triggers — see gtm and the GTM cookie consent guide.

What the order controls #

The banner recognises the googletagmanager.com loader (gtag/js or gtm.js) and holds it under category 2 Content Personalisation by default. The whole inline block is held when it names that address. In regions whose rule requires consent first, the tag waits until the visitor allows that category; it starts after Allow. A script placed above the banner snippet runs straight away.

Confirm the result #

View the page source: the banner snippet comes first in <head>, the GA4 tag after it. Before choosing, in a region whose rule requires consent first, _ga and _ga_<container-id> are absent; the held script shows type="javascript/blocked" in the Elements panel. After Allow, those cookies appear. Browser checks: plain-html; full procedure: verify-install.

Gotchas #

  • Google Consent Mode on. The googletagmanager.com loader then loads straight away with a denied signal until the visitor chooses. Judge by the cookies (_ga, _ga_<container-id>), not by whether the loader request appears. See Google Consent Mode v2.
  • Tags inside GTM. Gate them with consent triggers; on the New engine, recognised tags GTM fires are also held automatically. See the GTM cookie consent guide.
